title: Integration tests and property tests for uuencoding-multi
description:
Write a thorough integration test suite in tests/integration.rs and property tests.

Test oracle discipline: ALL expected values must come from external oracles (UNIX uudecode, Python uu module, or known-good test fixtures). Never use this crate's output as its own expected value.

Integration tests (tests/integration.rs):
  - Test fixture: create a 3-part multi-part UU sequence from a known file using UNIX uuencode split at the shell level; use hex!() literals for the byte content
  - End-to-end happy path: parse 3 subject lines, build PartCollection, reassemble, verify output matches oracle bytes
  - End-to-end with TOC (part 0): parse TOC, parse 3 data parts, reassemble, verify output
  - Out-of-order insertion: add parts 3, 1, 2; verify reassemble works
  - Missing middle part: add parts 1, 3 with total=3; verify is_truncated=true and missing_parts=[2]
  - Duplicate part rejected by PartCollection::add
  - Subject lines: test all format variants from MIME-zjr.1 with at least 2 real examples each
  - TOC parsing: at least 3 real TOC body samples (transcribed from real Usenet archives or constructed to match documented formats)

Property tests (proptest or quickcheck):
  - parse_subject does not panic on any arbitrary &str input (use proptest::arbitrary)
  - parse_toc does not panic on any arbitrary &[u8] input
  - PartCollection::add never panics regardless of input order

No test may use this crate to generate its own expected values. All multi-part byte sequences used as fixtures must be generated externally (uuencode shell command) and recorded as constants.

Quality gate:
  cargo fmt
  cargo clippy -p uuencoding-multi -- -D warnings
  cargo test -p uuencoding-multi

PARENT: MIME-zjr
